## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** — head `82900eb0d3034cbb26cc0b85dc9d0f497c5d39fb` (the head comment 6933089649 declares final). Card #33941, area o2-S. Read at 2026-11-16T23:58Z.

### Checklist conclusions

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. One closing line for the card, after the attribution lines. The card's done-when is met: the script has a self-test with a real two-branch conflict and a no-conflict case, and `area-lease.md` names the script. So the card closes whole. The full body has no closing verb next to any other number.
- **Premise.** The card says to build after PR #33938; the claim (6932009365) records it merged (`2af9c0af`). On `main` before this PR, no `scripts/pm/` script runs `git merge-tree` against PR heads.
- **Scope.** Two files: new `scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs` (+488) and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md` (+4/−4). The branch carries one merge of `origin/main` (`82900eb0`); the three-dot diff holds only these two files. The script is a standing tool run on every claim and push, not a one-off codemod.
- **Changeset.** Not owed. Neither path is in a published package (root `scripts/pm/**` and `.claude/**`), so `skip-changeset` is the right route, and `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- **Rule text (area-lease.md), read line by line.**
  - `Pre-claim deps:` drops the hot-file idle wait and points to the new line.
  - New line: run the tool before a claim and before every push; queue only on exit 1; on exit 3, meet the prerequisite and re-run. This matches the script's exit table.
  - Same-series start, in the AGENTS.md Multi-agent discipline item 2 trunk form, with no stacked PR. AGENTS.md L472–475 rules out a stacked series and names the trunk branch, so the line agrees with it.
  - Per-card test file, except where the AGENTS.md shared-harness rule applies (AGENTS.md L146–147, record 6583487846), in which case the overlap check decides. This is the wording the card's scope note 6896403681 asks for.
  - No issue numbers: `check-skill-id-lint` at head reads `118 file(s) clean`.
- **Paydown: each cut keeps a home (read at head).**
  - Dev self-declaration pointer → `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` L262 〈Definition of done〉, which every dev reads, and AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 (BREAKING / ADR-0087 there).
  - W0 "don't self-close" pointer → `execution-duties.md` L62 (已修交分诊或维护者关,⛔ 不自关). That line is scoped to the idle chores. What binds for W0 is the surviving sub-line 清单经维护者过目后落笔 (L25): nothing on the list is written before the maintainer's pass. Both homes hold.
  - Seat-move pointer → `seat-lifecycle.md` L43 (移座).
  - `check-skill-line-ratchet` at head: `area-lease.md is 71 lines (ceiling 71; headroom 0)`. No ceiling was raised, and the card permits none without a ruled raise.
- **Code read** (`overlap-check.mjs`; spot-read, not a full L2).
  - The exit table is `0` clean / `1` overlap / `2` usage / `3` cannot answer. Every unreadable state returns 3, never 0: no merge base, a failed `merge-tree`, a list or `/files` read that fails part-way, a fetch that fails.
  - Candidates are PRs whose `filename` or `previous_filename` meets the branch's change set; the branch's own PR is skipped by head ref or by sha.
  - A PR conflict counts only on a file the branch changed; the rest is printed as `not yours`.
  - `git --attr-source=<empty tree> merge-tree` bypasses the in-tree `os-regen` driver routing. The self-test pins this with a control leg: a plain merge-tree with the driver on exits 0, while the tool reports the conflict. On a git older than 2.40 the option is unknown, the call fails, and the answer is exit 3, not a false clean.
  - Dependency-free: node built-ins plus the repo's own `gh-pages.mjs` and `invoked-as.mjs`.
- **Self-test at head.** `node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs --self-test` → `✓ overlap-check self-test: 23 cases in 7 batteries pass.` (exit 0). It has a literal battery roster with per-battery floors, a roster-size pin, and a verdict handshake, as AGENTS.md 〈Writing a `--self-test`〉 requires. Fixtures: `refs/pull/7/head` is a real conflict, `8` touches the same file in another hunk, `9` touches a disjoint file.
- **Gates.** Check-runs on this head: 49 runs, 26 `success`, 23 `skipped`, 0 failure, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` aggregate, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are all `success`. The local 36-command ledger (`33941-gates-ran.txt`) is pinned to `7ec5d564`, not to this head, so I do not book it. Check-runs are the gate record. I re-ran four at this head, all green: the self-test, `check-skill-line-ratchet`, `check-skill-id-lint` and `check-self-test-wired`.

### Accepted deviations / observations

- D1: exit `3` is added beside the card's 0/1/2. Accepted: it keeps "could not look" from sharing a code with an answer, and the rule line tells the reader what to do on 3.
- D2: the self-test is not wired into CI (no root alias, no workflow step). Accepted under the lane's default-no rule for new gates; `check-self-test-wired` stays green because it counts only wired members. The cost is that nothing re-runs it after merge. Wiring it touches `.github/workflows/**`, so it needs a card and the maintainer's word.
- D3: the same-series line is reconciled to the AGENTS.md trunk form, not a literal "start on the previous card's branch". Accepted: AGENTS.md outranks this file.
- O1 (nit): `--attr-source` replaces only the in-tree attribute source. `.git/info/attributes` and `core.attributesFile` are still read. In this repo the driver routing sits in the committed `.gitattributes`, so the trap the tool guards against is covered.
- O2: the serial wording outside this card's surface still stands (`execution-duties.md` fold-or-serial; the hot-file queue in `seat-post-protocol.md` and `seat-lifecycle.md`). The PR body says so; the other hot-file cards, B–F, carry it.

### Contract review (L2) owed?

**Yes, and still open.** `.claude/**` is governed rules text, so it owes `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. At the time of reading, this head has only a claim: `l2-review#4`, comment 6933110417, head `82900eb0…`. There is no PASS record yet.

### Landing tier

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34512` reads **GOVERNED, Tier S**: `.claude/**` is hit once, and `scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs` is not on the register. Size is +492 / −4, under 3000. Once an at-tier PASS stands on this same head, the owning area lands it: ready, then the merge queue, with every check green. This review does not flip ready, arm auto-merge, or merge.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `82900eb0d3034cbb26cc0b85dc9d0f497c5d39fb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md + scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #33941 body and all five comments (scope note 6896403681, triage 6931095699, claims 6932009365 and 6932038090, dev report 6932726578), PR #34512 body, its two-file list and net diff, both PR comments, and the 49 check-runs on this head (26 success, 23 skipped, none failing, none pending). The PR's file list is exactly the two scoped files; nothing else is in the net diff against the PR base.

- Published accept sets and public surface: none change. Nothing under `packages/**`, `skills/**` or any published path is touched. Right.
- Rules-text accept set, `Pre-claim deps:` (area-lease.md line 33): the check no longer requires a named hot file to be idle; it defers to the new overlap-check line. This widens what an area may claim. Right: it is the maintainer's 2026-11-15 choice quoted in the card body, and the card names this file for it.
- New rule line 36 (run before a claim and before every push, queue only on exit 1, on exit 3 meet the prerequisite and re-run): matches card item 2 and the script's exit table. Right.
- New rule lines 40-41 (same-series start in the AGENTS.md §2 trunk form with no stacked PR; per-card test files except where the AGENTS.md shared-harness rule applies, then the overlap check decides queueing): the test-file half is the scope note's wording, and the AGENTS.md rule it defers to exists at head (ruling record 6583487846). Right. The series half is judged in ④ (N2).
- Three lines removed to pay the budget. The dev self-declaration pointer survives in `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` (Definition of done, present at head) and AGENTS.md Post-Task item 3; the seat-move pointer survives at `seat-lifecycle.md` line 43 (present). The W0 line (close per `execution-duties.md`, never on the area's own reading) survives as the W0 sub-line that the list is acted on only after the maintainer's pass, plus `execution-duties.md` line 62; that second home is scoped to the idle chore, so the prohibition is slightly narrower outside W0 than before. Accepted: the file's own header rule is to point, not copy, and the W0 closes remain behind the maintainer.
- Line budget: the file is 71 lines at head against a ratchet row of 71, row unchanged, no raise. Right; the card's "ruled raise" clause is not exercised.
- New internal tool surface (`scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs`): flags `--branch --base --remote --repo --pr --exclude-pr --json --self-test`; exit 0 clean, 1 overlap, 2 usage, 3 cannot answer; a tool-owned ref namespace `refs/overlap-check/pull/N`. Exit 3 is an addition to the card's three codes. Right: without it an unreadable state would share a code with an answer, and line 36 teaches all of 1 and 3.
- Verdict rule "a conflict against a PR head counts only on a file the branch changed": wrong in one case, see S1 in ④.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no. Agreed. The diff publishes nothing: `scripts/pm/**` and `.claude/**` ship in no package, so there is no changeset and the PR carries `skip-changeset`; the `Check Changeset` run on this head concluded success. No accept set of a published schema narrows or widens, so no `(narrowing)` arm applies. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, exit code 3: accepted (①).
- Deviation, self-test not wired into CI (no package alias, no workflow step): accepted for this card; the self-test gates on this head are green with the script outside their membership. Consequence to carry forward: no check-run on this head, or on any later one, executes the 23 cases, so the pass count is the dev's statement and the one property the tool's correctness rests on (an empty attribute source keeps a registered merge driver from hiding a conflict) has no standing evidence after a git upgrade. Escalated to the seat as a follow-up card: wire it, or record why not.
- Deviation, harness attribution comment in the PR body: not a contract matter.
- open_questions 1 (route to L2 at this head): answered by this record.
- open_questions 2 (same-series start against the AGENTS.md ban on a stacked series): option A stands. The line subordinates itself to AGENTS.md §2 and forbids the stacked PR, and AGENTS.md wins over this file. Wording nit N2 in ④.
- open_questions 3 (script name): A, `overlap-check.mjs`. No objection; nothing else in `scripts/pm` uses the name.
- out_of_scope finding (serial wording elsewhere still stands; "noted, not filed"): not accepted as noted-only. At head, `execution-duties.md` lines 32-35 still make fold-or-serial a mandatory answer with serial as the default and the later card waiting for MERGED, SKILL.md line 127 still says p0 does not exempt same-file serialisation, and area-lease.md itself sends the area to `execution-duties.md` for the claim (line 37) and for folding (line 46). An area seat therefore holds two answers for two queued cards on one hot file. area-lease.md is the mode-specific text and reads as the override, but no line says so. Escalated to the seat: file the follow-up, or point to the sibling hot-file card (B to F) that already carries it. Outside this diff, so not graded here.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No data access, no id materialisation, no in-app join in either file.
- Security: the tool reads through `gh api` GET and `git fetch` only, writes one ref namespace it owns, and takes its arguments from the seat that runs it. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

area-lease.md, against the card, the scope note and AGENTS.md at head:

- Lines 33 and 36 hold against the card and the tool: the exit codes named are the tool's, the path is the tool's, and "before every push" matches the header's "committed work only".
- Lines 40-41 hold against the scope note and AGENTS.md line 146.
- N1 (nit) — "认领前" has no change set to judge. Before a claim the card has no commits, so the default `--branch=HEAD` run compares an empty or unrelated change set, selects no candidate and exits 0; that 0 then stands in the claim comment's `Pre-claim deps:` line as if the hot file had been looked at. It never produces a wrong queueing decision under the ruling (no text, no textual overlap), and it is meaningful only for a same-series start, where the branch already has commits. Cost: one run and one read of every open PR's file list per claim. Follow-up, not a blocker: say which branch the pre-claim run takes, or have the tool say "empty change set" rather than "clean".
- N2 (nit) — "可从前卡分支起步" can be read as a fresh branch cut from the previous card's branch, which with a PR against main is the stacked series AGENTS.md §2 rules out (squash landing breaks the ancestry). The parenthetical trunk form and the ban on a stacked PR constrain it, and AGENTS.md wins, so the rule holds; "on the previous card's branch" (the card's own word) would close the reading. It also sits beside line 44 (the next card is taken only once the previous PR is in the merge queue), where pushing to that branch would dequeue it; the line does not say the trunk form is for cards claimed together.
- N3 (nit) — line 36 says "排队" without saying behind whom, and a conflict with `origin/main` (the tool's base leg, also exit 1) is cured by merging main, not by queueing. Two already-open PRs that conflict each read exit 1 on their next push with no tie-break named.

overlap-check.mjs, header sentence against code:

- Change set, base merge, candidate selection (renames by both names, own PR skipped by head ref and by head sha, `--exclude-pr`), the `--pr` path reading nothing from the API, the fetch into `refs/overlap-check/pull/N`, exit 3 on a missing merge base, an unreadable list, an unreadable file list or a failed fetch, and the deepen remedy naming the chosen remote: each agrees with its header sentence. `readAllPages` in `gh-pages.mjs` refuses a partial list, so a failed page cannot shorten the candidate set. Unknown git options or a refused merge fall to exit 3, never to 0.
- Self-test shape against AGENTS.md "Writing a --self-test": a frozen roster of seven named batteries with per-battery floors summing to the 23 cases the code registers, a roster-size pin, a refusal for an undeclared battery, and a verdict flag set after the success line that the dispatch checks. Agrees. The card's "Done when" (a real two-branch conflict and a no-conflict case) is met by the second and third batteries.
- S1 (should-fix) — a real conflict with a PR that renames a file the branch edits is classed "not yours" and the tool exits 0. `run()` keeps a PR-head conflict only when the conflicted path is in the branch's own change set (the `mine.has` filter on `m.conflicts`). When the PR renames `a.txt` to `moved.txt` and both sides edit the same lines, git reports the conflict at the rename destination, `moved.txt`, which the branch never changed by that name; the path goes to `notYours`, is printed as the PR's conflict with main, and does not move the exit code. The same happens when the PR renames a directory the branch adds a file under. This contradicts the header's "exit 0 no textual overlap ... with every open PR head that shares a file with the branch" and its claim that renames count by both names: `selectCandidates` picks the PR because of the rename and `run()` then discards the conflict it was picked for. The self-test covers rename only at candidate selection, never end to end. Effect: line 36 tells the area not to queue, and the conflict surfaces in the merge queue, which is the outcome the card exists to prevent; main is not put at risk. Fix direction: decide "not yours" by evidence rather than by name, for example count a PR-head conflict as the PR's own only when the same path also conflicts in a merge of the base with that PR head, or map each candidate's `previous_filename` to `filename` into the comparison set; add an end-to-end rename case to the CLI battery.
- N4 (nit) — the header cites AGENTS.md Multi-agent discipline §11 and `os-regen-merge.sh` for the driver trap, but the instrument those two prescribe is a throwaway bare clone that fetches both commits; the empty attribute source is a third instrument neither text names. It is not one of the two spellings §11 forbids, and its equivalence is argued and self-tested here, but see the unwired self-test under ③. A sentence in the header saying it differs from the prescribed recipe and why would stop a reader from "correcting" it.
- N5 (nit) — the refs under `refs/overlap-check/pull/` are never pruned and keep fetched PR histories alive in the shared object store.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1, open on this head; it earns a delta review of its fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-7xrx9z`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmP44onN8RMzsPMqjRq`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 (delta)

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** — head `5d8e2161d19dc039d2139444cc3bc5c66d50b6fe` (the head comment 6933674869 declares it final), superseding my ACCEPT 6933144692 at `82900eb0`. This is a delta read: what moved from `82900eb0` to this head, against the contract review 6933258205. Read at 2026-11-17T00:25Z.

### What moved

- Two commits on the card's files (`9908d7ed`, `2bebc350`) plus one merge of `origin/main` (`5d8e2161`).
- The two-dot diff from the old head also carries `main`'s own changes (#34472, #34485, #34498, #34491) through the merge. The three-dot diff against `main` is still exactly the two card files: `scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs` (+541) and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md` (+4/−4).

### S1 (should-fix): fixed, and the fix is proven

- **`run()` now judges "not yours" by evidence.** A conflict on a path in the branch's change set always counts. A conflict on any other path is `notYours` only when `merge-tree BASE × PR head` conflicts on that same path. Everything else counts. When the base × PR merge cannot be computed, the answer is exit 3, never 0.
- **New CLI cases.** PR 10 renames `a.txt` → `moved.txt` with the same line edited: exit 1, `moved.txt` under `conflicts`, `notYours` empty. `mine2` on a newer main against PR 7, conflicting only with that main: exit 0, with `a.txt` under `notYours`.
- **Ablation, run by me at this head.** I replaced the evidence filter with `const notYours = elsewhere;`. Exactly one case went red: "a PR renaming the file the branch edits … exits 1, counted as yours". With the code restored, the self-test reads `✓ overlap-check self-test: 26 cases in 7 batteries pass.` The cli battery floor moves 6 → 9 to match the three new cases.

### Nits carried in this head

- N5: fetched heads are now deleted in a `finally` (`update-ref -d`). Each ref is pushed to the cleanup list right after its fetch succeeds, so an early exit 3 cleans up too. Pinned by the case "no fetched PR head is left under refs/overlap-check/pull/".
- N1, N3 and N4 are answered in the header: before a claim the change set is empty, so the answer is 0 by construction; a base conflict means merge, not queue; and why the empty attribute source differs from the §11 bare-clone probe.
- In `area-lease.md`, the queue line now reads 「exit 1 排所列 PR 后,3 补前提重跑」. The file is 71/71 (`check-skill-line-ratchet` at this head), and `check-skill-id-lint` reads `118 file(s) clean`.
- N2 is carried as an accepted deviation. It matches my D3.

### Gates

Check-runs on this head: 48 runs, 26 `success`, 22 `skipped`, 0 failure, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` aggregate, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are all `success`. `Check Changeset` is `skipped` on both of its runs, which is not red, and nothing here publishes. The body now says the self-test is local only, which matches my D2 (no CI run executes it). That remains a follow-up for the seat, as the contract review's ③ says.

### Observation

- O3 (nit): the area-lease line says 排所列 PR 后. An exit 1 caused only by a base conflict lists no PR; the cure (merge the base) is in the script header, not in the rule line. A reader who runs the tool sees the base line printed, so this is not a rework item.

### Contract review (L2) owed?

**Yes: the delta review of S1 on this head.** Record 6933258205 is a PASS at `82900eb0`, with S1 open, and it states that S1 "earns a delta review of its fix". This head has no L2 record yet. Per `contract-review.md`, landing needs a same-form at-tier PASS on the current head with no open must-fix or should-fix.

### Landing tier

Unchanged. It is **Tier S** (`.claude/**` ×1; `scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs` is off the register; size is under 3000). ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5d8e2161d19dc039d2139444cc3bc5c66d50b6fe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md + scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

Delta review. The previous at-tier record is comment 6933258205 on head 82900eb0 (PASS, S1 open, nits N1 to N5, two escalations). Inputs read for this head: that record, all seven PR comments (the lane's final-head comment 6933674869 and the L1 delta 6933712371 included), the PR body, the PR file list, both scoped files whole at this head, the delta between the two heads restricted to the two scoped paths, AGENTS.md Multi-agent discipline item 11 at head, and all 48 check-runs on this head (26 success, 22 skipped, none failing, none pending). The PR file list is still exactly the two scoped paths; the three-dot diff against the PR base holds the same two files (+545 / -4). The other files in the two-dot diff between the heads are main's own, brought in by the merge commit, and are not judged. Nothing was built, run or checked out; every statement below about the tool's behaviour is from reading the code, and every pass count or ablation reading is the lane's and the L1's statement, not mine.

- Published accept sets and public surface: still none. The delta touches only the two scoped paths. Right.
- Rules text, area-lease.md line 36: the tail changes from "only exit 1 queues" to "exit 1 queues behind the listed PRs, exit 3 meets the prerequisite and re-runs". The accept set does not move: the same exit codes trigger the same two acts, and the line now says behind whom. The file is 71 lines at head, the ratchet row is untouched. Right.
- Verdict rule in `runOnce()` (the S1 fix): a PR-head conflict on a path in the branch's change set counts, as before. A conflict on any other path is `notYours` only when that same path is also in the conflict list of a merge of the base with that PR head; every other path counts.
